architecture_decisions.recommendation: Extended the existing preview panel to support PDF files using the native <object> HTML element, maintaining the same UI patterns as image previews
architecture_decisions.rationale: Reusing the existing PreviewPopup component ensures consistency with the established UI patterns and minimizes code duplication. The <object> element is the standard way to embed PDFs in browsers and provides native browser PDF rendering capabilities.
alternatives_considered: Creating a separate PDF-specific preview component
Implementing custom PDF rendering with JavaScript libraries

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added conditional logic to only enable PDF preview when UI and backend share the same host origin due to CSP restrictions
architecture_decisions.rationale: Content Security Policy (CSP) often restricts cross-origin object/embed tags for security reasons. By checking same-origin, we prevent broken previews and potential security issues when the UI is served from a different domain.
alternatives_considered: Implementing CORS headers to allow cross-origin PDF previews
Using proxy endpoints to serve PDFs from same origin
Disabling PDF preview entirely in cross-origin scenarios

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added click-to-open functionality for non-previewable file types in collection rows, making all files accessible with a single click
architecture_decisions.rationale: Previously, users had to navigate through multiple steps to open non-previewable files. This improves UX by providing consistent interaction patterns across all file types and reducing friction in file access.
alternatives_considered: Adding a separate 'Open' button for non-previewable files

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Enhanced file type detection logic to properly identify PDF files and determine previewability
architecture_decisions.rationale: Accurate file type detection is essential for showing appropriate previews and interactions. The system needed to distinguish between image previews, PDF previews, and non-previewable files.

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Updated CSS styles to accommodate PDF previews while maintaining visual consistency with existing previews
architecture_decisions.rationale: PDF previews may have different aspect ratios and rendering characteristics than images. The styling needed to ensure PDF previews fit properly within the existing preview panel layout.
alternatives_considered: Creating separate CSS for PDF previews
Using inline styles for PDF-specific adjustments

implementation_summary:
The implementation extends PocketBase's file preview system to support PDF files while enhancing general file handling. The approach leverages the existing PreviewPopup component architecture, adding PDF-specific rendering via the native <object> HTML element. This maintains UI consistency with image previews while providing browser-native PDF rendering capabilities.

Key design decisions include: 1) Reusing the existing preview infrastructure to minimize code duplication and maintain consistent UX patterns; 2) Implementing security-conscious same-origin checks for PDF previews due to CSP restrictions; 3) Adding click-to-open functionality for non-previewable files to improve user experience across all file types.

The solution integrates seamlessly with the existing codebase by extending rather than replacing components. File type detection logic was enhanced to properly identify PDFs and determine previewability. The changes are backward compatible, maintaining all existing functionality while adding new capabilities. The compiled asset updates ensure the UI changes are properly deployed in the production build.
